title: How to Make a Daiquiri That Doesn’t Fall Apart
subtitle: Simple, sharp, and unforgiving if you get lazy.
summary:
The Daiquiri is one of the simplest drinks you can make, and somehow one of the easiest to get wrong. It’s just rum, lime, and sugar — nothing to hide behind.

If you’re off by even a small amount, the whole drink shifts. Too much lime and it’s harsh. Too much sugar and it falls flat. When it’s right, though, it’s one of the cleanest, most refreshing cocktails you can make.

quick_mix.headline: Quick Mix
lines: Shake with ice, strain into a chilled glass

editorial_sections.title: This Is Where Ratios Actually Matter
editorial_sections.body:
If you want to understand cocktail balance, make a Daiquiri. There’s nowhere to hide here. Every small change shows up immediately.

This is the drink that teaches you how much a quarter ounce actually matters.

editorial_sections.title: Fresh Lime Is Not Optional
editorial_sections.body:
Bottled lime juice ruins this drink. It flattens everything and takes away the brightness that makes a Daiquiri work.

Fresh lime gives it that clean, sharp edge that keeps the drink from feeling heavy.

editorial_sections.title: Why Small Adjustments Matter
editorial_sections.body:
A Daiquiri isn’t forgiving. If you push the lime too far, it’s harsh. If you push the sugar too far, it gets dull.

That’s why starting with a solid ratio matters — and then adjusting slightly based on taste.

editorial_sections.title: What a Good Daiquiri Should Feel Like
editorial_sections.body:
It should feel bright, clean, and balanced from the first sip. You should taste the rum, but it shouldn’t overpower the citrus.

When it’s right, it’s crisp and refreshing without feeling thin.

steps: Add rum, lime juice, and simple syrup to a shaker.
Fill with ice and shake until well chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.
notes:
If the drink feels too sharp, add a touch more simple syrup. If it feels too sweet, increase the lime slightly. Small adjustments matter here.

Go deeper on balance and ratios in Bar Resources: Most Cocktails Fail Here (And It’s Not the Alcohol) — same backbone this drink lives on.
